items.text: This is a pretty key insight. Services businesses are always held back by their ability to deliver outcomes to customers. That scaling essentially only could come from headcount, and no matter how much demand you saw, there was always a finite amount of talent you could get for the problem you were going after. Not to mention, the customer generally always wants the work done faster, at a lower price, or at a higher quality. Agents entirely change the calculus here, because now we can scale output in a way that’s decoupled from the among of time that goes in. items.title: New research from Replit on scaling laws for agent swarms
items.text: New research from Replit on scaling laws for agent swarms. We show that scaling the number of agents can yield dramatic performance gains, but unlike traditional scaling laws, more compute doesn't necessarily translate into better results, and how agents organize themselves matters. - Given a fixed two-hour window, Opus 5.5 went from a 3.7x speedup on NumPy with one agent to 18.9x with 32 agents. - GPT-6.2 Astra was the strongest solo agent but exhibited negative scaling beyond 8 agents. - Models spontaneously developed different organizational structures. items.text: Part of the disconnect is that the name “data” massively undersells what it truly represents in model development. People who are not close to model development think of data as this inert commodity you buy and shovel into a model, like coal. In reality great data encodes incredibly high value knowledge, taste and expertise, often articulated and structured in ways that did not exist previously. This makes it one of THE fundamental building blocks for creating increasingly capable intelligence across domains. Data will continue to be incredibly central to the intelligence industry .
